item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is meaningfully closer to the frozen contract: it preserves FilesService.Add unchanged and adds the required replayable Upload API with explicit validation and established multipart helper reuse. B changes Add’s behavior and scope despite an explicit requirement not to do so.","reasons":["A preserves Add’s implementation and lower-level semantics; B eagerly reads and buffers every Add body, changing read timing, memory use, and reader-error semantics.","A explicitly rejects an empty filename and nil content before request construction. B delegates validation to multipartbody.NewFile rather than visibly enforcing both requirements.","A retains the existing Add test and adds focused multipart, validation, and retry tests. B replaces the existing Add test and does not add validation or source-reader-error coverage.","Both candidates fail the explicit requirement that Upload route through FilesService.Add: A duplicates Add’s request/response path, while B routes both methods through a new private add helper. This defect does not outweigh B’s additional contract violation of changing Add itself."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add’s option handling, request construction, response decoding, and missing-data error logic instead of calling Add.","No test covers propagation of a source-reader failure.","The retry test uses bytes.NewReader rather than a clearly non-replayable streaming source, so it weakly demonstrates the reported os.File/streamed-reader scenario."],"risks_b":["Changes Add behavior by buffering all caller-built bodies, directly violating the preservation requirement and potentially increasing memory use or changing when errors occur.","Upload does not call Add, contrary to the required layering.","No visible tests cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures, and the original Add test is replaced rather than retained without weakening coverage in its original form."]}
